evidence_items.explanation: In Q1 2026 Anthropic's revenue ($4,731 million) exceeded its entire compute and infrastructure expense ($3,387 million), which also covers research and training. So serving customers did not cost more than the revenue it brought in.

metric_scope.metric: revenue versus total compute and infrastructure expense

derived.formula: 4,731 - 3,387 = 1,344 million of revenue above all compute and infrastructure costs

evidence_items.locator: MD&A, Operating Expenses, Compute and Infrastructure

receipt.public_excerpt:
Compute and infrastructure expenses primarily consist of costs attributable to operating our technology

infrastructure, which supports the full range of workloads for our models, including research, model

development, serving customers, and internal usage of Claude.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms that the compute line in e1 includes research and training as well as serving customers, so the cost of serving customers alone was lower still.

evidence_items.locator: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, Supplemental Operating Expense Information table (columns: 2023, 2024, 2025, H1 2025, H1 2026)
evidence_items.explanation: Cost of revenue was $2,773 million against $4,585 million of revenue in 2025, and $2,380 million against $16,286 million in the first half of 2026. Both show positive gross margins. These periods fall outside the Q1 2026 target, so this is context.

receipt.public_excerpt: Broadcom (AVGO) leads at about $161 billion, ahead of Google (GOOG, GOOGL) at about $115 billion, Amazon (AMZN) at $110 billion, and Microsoft (MSFT) at about $45 billion.

evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic's noncancelable commitments to Google, Amazon and Microsoft totalled about $270 billion as of the S-1. This partly informs the $718 billion figure but does not cover OpenAI and post-dates the post.

unresolved_gaps: The $718 billion total for both companies' commitments to Microsoft, Google and Amazon could not be verified from primary sources.
OpenAI's revenue and cost of serving customers were not reviewed.
Anthropic still had a GAAP operating loss in Q1 2026 and raised outside capital, so the 'needs funding' part alone is not contradicted for that quarter.
